topic: Hasselgren Minkowski conservative rasterization AABB dilation vs pixel-center sub-pixel line dropout rig
topic_zh: Hasselgren 闵可夫斯基半像素保守光栅化扩张对比像素中心点采样亚像素断线与体素漏洞
scope: Deterministic Hasselgren, Akenine-Moller & Ohlsson (2005) Minkowski sum conservative rasterization (R_cons = r + h*(|n_x| + |n_y|)) versus naive pixel-center point sampling and 4-corner Separating Axis Theorem (SAT) interval testing across 17 pixel center distances (d in [0.00, 0.80] px). No neural voxel completion execution.

protocol.function: R_cons = r + h·(|n_x| + |n_y|) = 0.20 + 0.70 = 0.9000 px → 17 / 17 Intersected Pixels Captured

robustness.name: Sampled 17 intersected pixel boxes capture 100% of sub-pixel diagonal wire crossings without dropout

good_fit: GPU 3D surface voxelization (VXGI, collision SDFs), sub-pixel CAD wireframes, power lines, and watertight occlusion culling
Explaining why standard pixel-center point sampling drops 12/17 (70.59%) of pixels touched by a r=0.20px diagonal wire
Shifting edge planes outward by the pixel square L₁ support radius Δd = h·(|n_x| + |n_y|) = 0.7000 px
Replacing 4-corner Separating Axis Theorem (SAT) vertex loops with a 3-op Minkowski L₁ norm support function
not_for: Large opaque interior triangles where standard non-dilated hardware rasterization is desired
Watertight shared interior edges between adjacent triangles (where Top-Left tie-breaking avoids double overdraw)
Neural point-cloud or voxel occupancy completion networks
1D audio signal processing without 2D/3D spatial rasterization
